nba_directive.reason_text: This client has a 2.25% first mortgage — a rate that almost certainly cannot be improved by a straight refinance, making Fed-vs-mortgage education critical to redirect the conversation toward realistic options while protecting their existing low rate. Anchoring them to how mortgage pricing actually works (10-year Treasury, not Fed funds) and reframing any cash-out need as a HELOC/second lien is the high-leverage move here.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open with the Fed-vs-mortgage education before anything else
  - Text them directly: 'Quick thing worth knowing — mortgage rates don't actually follow the Fed rate. They track the 10-year Treasury, and any anticipated Fed cuts are already priced into today's rates, so waiting for Fed moves won't move your mortgage rate the way you might expect'
  - This reframe alone separates you from the 95%+ of bankers who never say it

- Protect their 2.25% rate — do NOT pitch a cash-out refi
  - Their $2,293/mo P&I at 2.25% on a $227,706 balance is a rate they will never see again
  - A cash-out refi would replace that rate with today's market rate, costing them significantly more per month on the entire balance
  - Never present this as a refinance option

- Pivot to HELOC / second lien if they have a cash need
  - Frame it as: 'We can leave your 2.25% completely untouched and put a second lien behind it'
  - If they carry any credit card debt, ask for the balances — then show the math: credit cards run 25–30% APR; a HELOC rate, even at today's levels, is a fraction of that cost
  - Compute and present: monthly interest they're paying on card balances vs. what a HELOC payment would be on the same amount

- Anchor to their specific financial pain
  - Ask one direct question: 'What were you hoping to accomplish — lower the payment, pull cash out, or something else?'
  - Once they name the pain, reframe the HELOC as the precise solution to that pain, not a generic product pitch

- Carry a break-even / savings number into the reply
  - You don't have their card balances yet, so coach them to share those: 'If you tell me what you're carrying on cards, I can show you the exact monthly savings and how fast this pays for itself'
  - Do not invent a savings figure — build it live once they respond

- Secure the next step in this same text thread
  - End with a binary close: 'Want me to run the numbers on a second lien, or easier to jump on a 10-minute call this week?'
  - Do not go silent after one message — if no reply in 24 hours, follow up with the specific savings question, not another equity blast
